subject: Security checkpoint: private deployment readout & questionnaire kickoff
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Lewis <timothy.lewis@medlinkhealth.com>, security+procurement@medlinkhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security checkpoint: private deployment readout & questionnaire kickoff

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to align on MedLink's risk profile and deployment constraints. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Recap from our conversation:
- Compliance posture: Redwood is currently undergoing SOC 2 Type II (in flight; targeted report Q1 2029). We can provide control mappings and SSAE bridge artifacts in the interim.
- Data residency & privacy: we support region-restricted deployments (US regions) and can sign a BAA for HIPAA workloads. GDPR controls are supported for EU-hosted deployments — we discussed US-only scope for now.
- Deployment options we covered (summary):
  * Option A — Hosted + VPC peering: fastest onboarding, private egress, logs in customer-controlled workspace. Not air-gapped.
  * Option B — Dedicated (private VPC): reserved GPU capacity, private control-plane connectivity, stronger isolation for regulated workloads.
  * Option C — On-prem / air-gapped bundle: full offline install for highest isolation (longer lead time for installation, verification, and support).

Ask / next steps:
1) Please return the vendor security questionnaire (attached) to security+procurement@medlinkhealth.com with any timeline constraints. I’ve attached a lightweight overlay sketch of how Redwood maps into a customer VPC (redwood_vpc_overlay_sketch.png).
2) Ben (cc’d) will follow with a short tech note on isolation and audit log handling.
3) If MedLink wants an air-gapped estimate, we can scope an engineering install runbook — estimate 6–12 weeks from kickoff depending on procurement and on-site access.
4) Proposed next meeting: technical deep-dive (network + auth + KMS) — can you do Thurs 9/14 at 10am PT?

Attachments: redwood_vpc_overlay_sketch.png

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks for the summary, that matches our notes. I’m attaching the MedLink vendor security questionnaire (xlsx) — please complete and return. A couple of clarifying items up front so we can prioritize internally:
- For SOC 2 in-flight evidence: what interim artifacts can you share now (control mappings, SOC scoping doc, management letter)?
- KMS/HSM: do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) in the private deployment? If so, which providers and delivery model (cloud KMS, HSM appliance integration)?
- Audit logs: what's the default retention and can we configure a non-exportable write-once store?
- Air-gapped installs: any client references and a high-level timeline?

We’d like the completed questionnaire back by EOD 9/20 to keep procurement moving. If possible, include a sketch of the private deployment topology (we saw the overlay but would like a version annotated with firewall/egress controls).

Tim — appreciate the fast turnaround. Quick answers below and attached a matrix that maps features to deployment options (redwood_privdeploy_matrix.pdf). I’ll fill the questionnaire and return a completed copy by EOD 9/14 as a first pass; Ben will provide technical detail where needed.

Interim artifacts we can provide now:
- Control mapping document (SOC control families covered; preliminary scope)
- Architecture diagram with annotated firewall/egress and KMS references (link below and attached matrix)
- BAA template and data processing addenda for HIPAA/GDPR

KMS/HSM:
- Customer-managed keys: supported in Dedicated and Private installs. We support AWS KMS CMKs, Azure Key Vault, and can integrate with on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11 or partner connectors.

Audit logs:
- Audit/event logs are available for all deployment modes and can be routed to customer-managed sinks (CloudWatch/Datadog/Splunk) or uploaded to a write-once archive. Retention is configurable; we’ll document options in the questionnaire.

Air-gapped installs:
- Typical timeline: initial scoping + procurement (2–4 weeks) then on-site install + verification (4–8 weeks). Total 6–12 weeks depending on approvals and network/access constraints. We have two past on-prem references for HIPAA customers; Ben can provide redacted contact points once NDA is in place.

Drive diagram (annotated): https://drive.google.com/redwood/diagrams/priv-deploy-sketch
Attached: redwood_privdeploy_matrix.pdf

I’ll upload a completed questionnaire draft by 9/14 and we can iterate. If 9/14 works for you for the deep-dive, I’ll calendar and include our infra lead.

Thanks,
Sean

Timothy — a few technical notes from the infra/security side that will help answer items in the questionnaire and guide the deep dive:

Short technical clarifications:
- Network isolation: for Dedicated/Private we recommend dedicated subnets with explicit egress NATs and a customer-controlled firewall or transit gateway. All control-plane calls are TLS mutual-auth; data plane can be restricted to internal CIDRs.
- KV cache & persistence: Redwood’s in-memory KV cache is ephemeral by default. Persistent caches are optional and are placed in customer-managed storage in Private deployments.
- Patching/updates in air-gapped installs: commodities (OS, runtime) are delivered via signed bundles — install requires a controlled maintenance window. Remote health telemetry can be disabled on request; local observability agents remain for on-site ops.
- Audit logs: we can push to a customer-managed SIEM using secure forwarders. If a write-once immutable store is required we support S3 Object Lock or equivalent append-only stores behind an access control layer.

Caveats for air-gapped model:
- Support SLAs differ because remote debug is limited — we provide runbooks and a remote debug token flow that you can enable for short windows.
- Third-party dependency licensing and updates need an explicit acceptance window (we’ll list packages that require occasional updates).

I’ll prepare a 1-page network isolation sketch to append to the questionnaire and bring it to the call if that’s helpful.

-Ben
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
